question:
How should modules be organized so that the software stays easy to maintain, and how can an existing badly structured program be improved without its users noticing any difference?

Answer with a list of guidelines. After each guideline, cite the source it comes from: the path of the SWEBOK file if you have it, otherwise a verbatim quote of at least 8 words from the passage, in the form (source: ...).
answer:

# Guidelines
- Minimize complexity throughout software construction by using [SWEBOK excerpt 7d6058e5a9e6b26a0e56], achieved through standards, modular design, and other specific techniques — because [SWEBOK excerpt e80657af9ba5ce24b064] working memory over long periods. (source: root/Software Design and Construction Fundamentals/Software Construction and Code Complexity Management/Software Construction Fundamentals and Practices/Software Construction Fundamentals.md; root/Software Design and Construction Fundamentals/Software Construction and Code Complexity Management/Software Construction Tools and Anticipating Change.md) [JEV 0.96]
- Anticipate and embrace change when constructing software. [SWEBOK excerpt 4ade4049c614110de336], which is particularly important as today's business environments require [SWEBOK excerpt dc76c209d05090e43e05]. (source: root/Software Design and Construction Fundamentals/Software Construction and Code Complexity Management/Software Construction Tools and Anticipating Change.md) [JEV 0.96]
- Apply the SOLID principles ([SWEBOK excerpt f2d1ea5d4fd0dd69e373]) for class design, and the SOFA principles ([SWEBOK excerpt 63d8c6ab4741cf142393]) for method design when organizing modules in object-oriented systems. (source: root/Software Design Methodologies and Approaches/Data-Centered, Object-Oriented, and User-Centered Design.md) [JEV 0.97]
- Use component-based design (CBD) to decompose a software system into [SWEBOK excerpt 6948ce9cb44f8d4bad74], so that each component can be developed, understood, and maintained independently. (source: root/Software Design Methodologies and Approaches/Data-Centered, Object-Oriented, and User-Centered Design.md) [JEV 0.97]
- Apply general design strategies such as divide-and-conquer, stepwise refinement, and top-down vs. bottom-up decomposition to structure modules. Structured (function-oriented) design identifies major software functions and elaborates them in a top-down manner, keeping module responsibilities clear and focused. (source: root/Software Design Methodologies and Approaches/Design Strategies and Structured Approaches/Design Strategies and Function-Oriented Methods.md; root/Software Design Methodologies and Approaches/Design Strategies and Structured Approaches/Structured Design and Top-Down Function Decomposition.md) [JEV 0.95]
- Record design rationale — including prior assumptions, alternatives considered, trade-offs analyzed, and reasons for rejected options — because although design decisions may be obvious to the current team, they become unclear to those who later modify or maintain the system. Recording rationale [SWEBOK excerpt a07a0ae76ebc0faea520]. (source: root/Software Design Concerns, Documentation, and Modeling/Recording Design Rationale for System Maintainability.md; root/Software Design Methodologies and Approaches/Design Strategies and Structured Approaches/Design Rationale and Software Design Strategies.md) [JEV 0.97]
- Continue capturing rationale for changes made during maintenance activities, because doing so contributes to the software's long-term viability. (source: root/Software Design Concerns, Documentation, and Modeling/Recording Design Rationale for System Maintainability.md) [JEV 0.98]
- Improve a badly structured program's internal structure through refactoring — a reengineering technique that reorganizes a program without changing its observable behavior — in order to improve internal structure and maintainability without users noticing any difference. (source: root/Software Maintenance and Configuration Management/Software Maintenance, Evolution, and Quality Assurance/Refactoring and Reverse Engineering in Software Development.md) [JEV 0.96]
- Use refactoring to reduce [SWEBOK excerpt 2c0775222e306edb53f3] Agile contexts with continuous integration, the code should [SWEBOK excerpt 44dcc5e80c12bea96aa9], managing [SWEBOK excerpt b86ce486560e62445e18]. (source: root/Software Maintenance and Configuration Management/Software Maintenance, Evolution, and Quality Assurance/Refactoring and Reverse Engineering in Software Development.md) [JEV 0.97]
- Use function-based (structured) design measures — obtained by analyzing functional decomposition and represented in structure charts — or object-oriented design measures based on class diagrams to quantitatively assess and evaluate the quality and structure of a software design. (source: root/Software Design Quality Evaluation and Assessment/Design Analysis and Quality Metrics/Software Design Metrics and References/Software Design Measures and Evaluation Methods.md) [JEV 0.96]
